<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via computeLayeredRlsFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin), getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dfbc73165a46da066dc89b0aeb46a8fba7628f62` — the merge of head `2b176bd2e614b180ddd7767f850f11a52f34463e` into base `02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dfbc73165a46da066dc89b0aeb46a8fba7628f62 && git checkout dfbc73165a46da066dc89b0aeb46a8fba7628f62
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef 2b176bd2e614b180ddd7767f850f11a52f34463e && git checkout -B drift-repro 02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef && git merge --no-ff 2b176bd2e614b180ddd7767f850f11a52f34463e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 02bec6ca86e9f1237a3f82a9efff9cb3a53562ef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e7221cba7058cb0e9c4a3f541e56f52d1003d0e8`
Local-runs: none

**Inputs read:** card #23009 (body and all 5 comments: the cross-lane request 6123462901, the claim 6126106500, the two `os-dev-report`s 6137424762 and 6137777568, the seat's answer 6137605804); PR #23144 body, its 11-file list and the diff against `main` (merge base `21c86444e`, +633/−40, matching the API diff); the 46 check-runs on the head; `origin/main` at `d206d08ca` and the head via `git show`. The seat's own review and answer were treated as claims to test, not evidence.

**Check-runs on the head, as read at 2026-10-13T03:50Z:** 28 completed/success, 10 in_progress, 8 completed/skipped, 0 failures. Success: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Check Changeset` (×2), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, and the four card/branch/single-writer guards (×2 each). In progress: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/6)` through `(6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. Skipped: `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, the sharded `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, one `Auto Label`, one `Check PR Size`. The verdict below rests on the diff; the pending runs are recorded, not relied on.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.**

1. `@objectstack/spec/data` gains four exports (`api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each +4, consistent with the barrel): `RLS_DENY_FILTER` (const), `COMPOSED_READABLE_IDS_BRAND` (const), `ComposedReadableIds` (interface), `isComposedReadableIds` (function); `ReadableIds` gains the member `compose`. **Right** — a pure widening, every member documented.
2. `RLS_DENY_FILTER` (spec, `readable-ids.ts:153`): frozen, value `{ id: '__rls_deny__:00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' }`, byte-identical to the literal removed from `rls-compiler.ts:680` on `main`. Typed `Readonly` over `{ id: string }`. Closed against forgery (identity is the test; nothing but the reference matches), against copies (a spread or clone is a fresh object: zero rows, not the sentinel — fail-safe) and against JSON (same). `markFilterSubtreeProvenance` no-ops on a frozen subtree and unmarked withholds (`filter-subtree-provenance.ts:163-165`, `:183`), so the sentinel never carries an `'author'` vouch. **Right.**
3. `@objectstack/plugin-security` keeps `export const RLS_DENY_FILTER` under its published `Record` type, bound to the spec object (`rls-compiler.ts:690`); `index.ts:12` re-exports it unchanged. ADR-0139 D2 step 2 anchors the sentinel at `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts#RLS_DENY_FILTER`; that symbol still exists on the head, so the ADR's anchor resolves (`check:adr-symbol-anchors` runs inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, success). One definition in the tree: `git grep __rls_deny__` outside tests and CHANGELOGs hits the spec literal plus prose that already exists on `main` (`lint/validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts:27`, `explain-engine.ts:205-208,:2405`, `explain.zod.ts:144,:152,:381,:390`) — none is a second value. **Right.**
4. `COMPOSED_READABLE_IDS_BRAND` is `Symbol.for('objectstack.filter.readableIds.composed')`, distinct from `READABLE_IDS_BRAND`; `compose` defines it non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable and freezes the leaf. JSON, `structuredClone`, spread and `Object.assign` all drop it (pinned). A global-registry symbol is forgeable by in-process code holding the key — the same posture the E1 leaf chose and documents (a duplicated package instance must resolve the key), and what closes the forge is the door, not the brand: `assertListComparandShapes` admits only `isReadableIds` under `admitReadableIds` (`filter-comparand-shape.ts:1089`), so a composed leaf, forged or real, handed in from outside is refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 as a non-list comparand (pinned). **Right, with the brand's forgeability stated as inherited design, not a new hole.**
5. `ReadableIds.compose(leaf, scope)` — three refusals, each a `TypeError`, in this order: `leaf` not a branded `ReadableIds` (a composed leaf, a spread copy, `{ object }`, `null`, a string all refused; pinned); `scope` not `undefined` and not a non-null, non-array object (`null`, `[]`, a string, `0`, `false` refused; pinned); `scope === RLS_DENY_FILTER` by identity, a copy of it composing as an ordinary scope (pinned, and ablation 3a shows the pin reds without the check). **Right in substance; one wording defect, see ③ item A2.**
6. `isComposedReadableIds`: own brand key holding exactly `true`, `object` a non-empty string, an own `scope` key holding `undefined` or a non-null non-array object; `null`, primitives, arrays, prototype-inherited brands, a missing `scope` key and every copy answer `false` (pinned, hand-built shapes included). **Right as a recogniser of what `compose` builds.** Its TSDoc's universal sentence is not: see ③ item A1.
7. `isReadableIds` is byte-identical to `main` (diffed the function body: IDENTICAL), so it answers exactly as before for every input. A composed leaf built by `compose` carries only the composed brand, so `isReadableIds(composed)` is `false` and `isComposedReadableIds(ReadableIds.of(x))` is `false` (pinned). **Right.** The H5 choice (own brand, not both) is the safe reading of D2's "still branded": ablation 3b shows both brands would let the door admit a forged composed leaf.

**The identity switch in `plugin-security` — can a deny be lost? No.** Every producer whose answer can reach `getReadFilter`'s top-level return now returns the reference, and no copy is made on the way:

- in `getReadFilter` itself (`security-plugin.ts:5857` principal-less, `:5873` sharing-scope throw, `:5895` on-behalf-of, `:5906` zero permission sets, `:5933` resolution throw);
- Layer 0: `tenantLayer0FilterOf` deny (`tenant-layer.ts:177`); Layer 1: the compiler's own deny (`rls-compiler.ts:1064`, already by reference on `main` at `:1056`) and the dropped-policy deny (`security-plugin.ts:8197`); the unresolvable-master deny (`:8850`);
- `andComposeLayers` (`tenant-layer.ts:249`) hands back the single non-null layer by reference and builds a fresh `$and` only when two constrain, so the sentinel surfaces at the top level exactly when it is the only constraining layer — which is what the changeset now says. The CBP chain-cycle, depth-bound and master-sharing-failure answers `{ fk: { $in: [] } }` and plugin-sharing's `{ id: '__deny_all__' }` are zero-row answers that are not the sentinel, as the changeset and the PR body say.
- `isTenantWallDenial` (`:789`, `filter === RLS_DENY_FILTER`) has one caller, `organizationWallRefusal` (`:8564`), whose `callerWall` and `delegatorWall` come from `computeWriteTenantCheckFilter` → `computeLayeredRlsFilter(...).layer0` → `tenantLayer0FilterOf` — the reference, untouched: the verified-owner read bypass (`:8268`) is guarded by `!isWrite` and so never rewrites a write's `layer0`. The no-active-organization write wall therefore fires exactly as before, and a future spread at the wall reds the write-refusal suite (ablation 2: 10 red). `explain-engine.ts:187` still decides by value, which stays correct.
- Within `plugin-security` all three readers bind through `./rls-compiler.js` (`security-plugin.ts:88`, `tenant-layer.ts:10`, `explain-engine.ts:57`): one module graph, so the CJS/ESM dual-copy miss noted by the dev cannot reach `isTenantWallDenial`. It can reach E2 (objectql loading another build of spec) and is fail-safe there; carried to #22861, rightly.

**Consumers that now receive the frozen object where they used to get a copy.** The CRUD middleware marks it `'policy'` (a no-op on frozen input, which withholds) and sets `ast.where` to it by reference or wraps it in a fresh `$and` (`:4244-4259`); the compiler's frozen deny already took that path on `main`, so the engine's lowering has tolerated a frozen `where` before this PR, and spec's lowering is copy-on-write (`filter-lowering.ts:60`). `service-analytics` (`plugin.ts:672` → `resolveReadScopes` → `compileScopedFilterToSql`) reads; `computeControlledByParentFilter` hands the master filter to a system `ql.find` `where` (`:8907`); `explain-engine` publishes it. A grep of `objectql/src`, `core/src`, `service-analytics/src`, `plugin-security/src` and `plugin-sharing/src` (non-test) for in-place writes (`$and.push`, `Object.assign` onto a where, `delete` on a where, indexed assignment on `where`/`readFilter`/`scope`) finds none. The `ISecurityService.getReadFilter` contract already forbids holding the returned object across requests and says nothing that promises a mutable copy. The one behaviour change — an editor of the returned deny now gets a `TypeError` — is stated in the changeset; it holds in strict-mode code (every ESM module, TS-emitted CJS), while a sloppy-mode consumer would see a silent no-op instead. Note only.

**Could a test or gate pass while an identity, a refusal or a recogniser is wrong?** Identities: every pin is `toBe` against the spec export, driven through the public method (14 cases), and ablations 1 and 2 show `toEqual` pins stay green while `toBe` pins red. Refusals: each of the three has a pin; ablation 3a reds the sentinel one. Recognisers: copies, clones, hand-built shapes and the door's refusal are pinned. **One gap:** nothing pins a value carrying BOTH brands, which is the case the TSDoc's disjointness sentence is wrong about (③ A1). `isReadableIds`'s unchanged answers rest on an unchanged body, not on a pin; acceptable, since the body is byte-identical.

**The case-set.** No file at the head names `READABLE_IDS_CASES` or `readable-ids-conformance` (grep: zero hits in `packages` and `scripts`); nothing shipped imports or presumes the case-set. The only forward references are TSDoc sentences naming D3's driver conformance suite as a future builder of the composed leaf. See ③ C for the closing line.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23009-rls-deny-sentinel-composed-readable-ids.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `@objectstack/plugin-security` **patch**; `.changeset/pre.json` is `mode: pre`, `tag: next` on both trees. **Right.** The spec entry widens (five new members, nothing removed or renamed), which is at least `minor` under the Post-Task Checklist and the no-major gate's pre-mode rule; nothing breaking, so no migration or ADR-0087 marker is owed and none is present (`check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major` pass on the head). `plugin-security` keeps its export name and published type, and `getReadFilter`'s signature is unchanged; the deny paths now return a frozen singleton the compiler path already returned — a fix, `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening: new exported members of the published spec data entry)` in the changeset and on PR line 2 matches the published change and the claim's line verbatim. The changeset body read against the head: the headline, the FROM → TO bullet, the identity bullet (its enumeration of sentinel returns matches the producer trace above, and its "not every zero-row answer is the sentinel" sentence is true and deliberately non-exhaustive), the composed-leaf bullet and the `isReadableIds` bullet are true, except the phrase "a scope that is not a plain filter object" shares the wording defect of ③ A2.

### ③ Boundary flags

**A. Shipped-sentence defects found on the head (the FAIL).**

- **A1 — `isComposedReadableIds`'s TSDoc claims a universal disjointness the code does not enforce.** The docblock (`readable-ids.ts`, the recogniser) says "Disjoint from `isReadableIds`: no value answers `true` to both." A hand-built object carrying an own `READABLE_IDS_BRAND: true` and an own `COMPOSED_READABLE_IDS_BRAND: true` with `object: 'x'` and an own `scope: undefined` answers `true` to both (both recognisers check only their own key, the value `true`, `object`, and the composed one `scope`); both keys are `Symbol.for` registry keys, so any in-process code can build it. The consequence is fail-closed wherever `isReadableIds` is asked (objectql's `refuseUncomposedReadableIds`, a D3 driver refusal), and a driver asking `isComposedReadableIds` first would compile the forger's scope — no wider than a single-brand forge already could at a driver called directly, so this is not a new leak. It IS a declared property the runtime does not deliver, in text that ships in the `.d.ts` (Prime Directive 10: keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement), and it is the exact question this review was asked. The module header's "DISJOINT" sentence is qualified ("`isReadableIds` answers `false` for a composed leaf") and holds. **Remedy, either closes it:** (a) make `isComposedReadableIds` answer `false` for a value that also carries an own `READABLE_IDS_BRAND` (one line; a double-branded value then resolves as uncomposed and is refused, fail-closed, whichever recogniser is asked first) and pin that value in the disjointness block of `readable-ids.test.ts`; or (b) narrow the sentence to what holds: no leaf either factory builds, and no copy of one, answers `true` to both; a hand-built value carrying both brands is refused as uncomposed wherever `isReadableIds` is asked. (a) is the better contract, since E2 and the drivers may ask the recognisers in either order.
- **A2 — "plain" overstates two refusals** (fix in the same round; not alone a FAIL): `compose`'s `@throws` ("neither `undefined` nor a plain, non-array object"), `isComposedReadableIds`'s docblock ("a plain, non-array object") and the changeset ("a scope that is not a plain filter object"). `isComposableScope` accepts any non-null, non-array `typeof 'object'` value — a `Date`, a `Map`, a class instance pass. The repo's `filter.zod.ts:2317` uses "plain object" in this loose sense too, so the intent is clear, but a `.d.ts` reader cannot see that: either say "a non-null, non-array object" or test the prototype the way objectql's `findReadableIds` does.

**B. The dev's flags (report 6137424762 `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`, report 6137777568 `deviations`) and the seat's disposition (6137605804).**

- Case-set not in the PR; PR line 1 `Part of` → the seat ruled Q1 = B and the patch round made line 1 `Fixes #23009`. Disposition judged in C below: right.
- Surface: `security-plugin.ts` edited at `:8190`/`:8842` (deny returns that reach `getReadFilter` through `andComposeLayers`), a docblock moved onto `isTenantWallDenial`, a paragraph added to `getReadFilter`'s docblock, a stale comment in `resolveCbpRelation` corrected; the import block untouched; nothing outside the claim's file list. Within the claim's "deny returns and the sentinel recogniser" reading and needed by the acceptance line. Right.
- H3: an aliasing `const` under the plugin's published `Record` type rather than a named re-export, so the plugin's export type does not narrow. Verified at `rls-compiler.ts:690`; the ADR anchor resolves. Right.
- The identity test's engine double carries no `findOne` instead of growing `engine-double-contract.pinned.json`. Verified in the test (`find` only, no deny path reads a row). Right.
- Env-var listing before the overnight rule: names only, values replaced by `sed`; no value printed. Noted; nothing to dispose.
- Commit attribution per AGENTS.md's model-free trailer. Not this review's surface.
- Coverage: the full `@objectstack/spec` suite NOT MEASURED locally (585 s cap); `Test Core` 1–6 are in progress on the head. The pins that matter to this contract (`readable-ids.test.ts`, the identity file, `tenant-layer.test.ts`) were run and are read here from the diff; the verdict does not depend on the pending runs.
- Patch-round deviations: the changeset's false engine sentence reworded to the ADR's prescription (true now: E2 is not landed, and the sentence says what D2 step 2 has the engine do); "not every zero-row answer is the sentinel" kept non-exhaustive (correct: the CBP `{ fk: { $in: [] } }` answers exist); PR-body edits beyond the three named; `post-stamped` ack of the docs-drift comment; labels left as found. All right.
- Out-of-scope findings: the CJS/ESM dual-copy identity miss and plugin-sharing's `__deny_all__` passthrough → carried to #22861: right (fail-safe here, E2's to measure; see ① for why it cannot reach `isTenantWallDenial`). `explain-engine.ts:178-186` docblock still says producers spread the constant → carried to #15194: right (module-private, value test still correct, epic territory; the prose is now stale on the head, so the carrier must not be lost). The prose hits naming the value → "one definition holds": right; every hit pre-exists on `main` and documents the published value.

**C. Both open questions, and the closing line.**

- **Q1 (where the case-set lands) = B, the case-set lands with the driver suites (E3/E4), zero ledger rows.** Right. The gate's own text makes a classified case-set red until every driver runs it, and its only other remedy is a maintainer-agreed ledger row, so the fold-in's second half could not land green by an author's act; D3's sentence ("the leaf joins the per-driver conformance case-sets") still holds under B. The seat correctly names the deviation from ADR-0139's E2 row, leaves the record unedited, and says the maintainer can overturn it. Two things to keep visible: the pointer 6137585321 on #22788 that carries the re-route is outside this review's inputs and was not read; and the card's original filed scope was the sentinel alone — the case-set entered by the seat's own acceptance of the cross-lane request (6126106500) and left by the seat's own ruling, both on the card, so the card's record is complete.
- **Q2 (collapse `deny AND x` to the sentinel) = A, composites stay composite.** Right for this card: not asked, it changes the shape of a published scope (the analytics raw-SQL scope), and a composite composes to a subquery that matches nothing — fail-safe. Carried to #22861 as a measurable follow-up.
- **The closing line `Fixes #23009` fits** with the case-set moved: the card's body (one declaration in spec's `data` entry with D2 step 2 named as its reader, `plugin-security` importing the object and holding no second literal, `Clause-②: yes`, one changeset, the identity pin on the compiler's emit) and the accepted amendment (every `getReadFilter` deny return the spec sentinel by reference, pinned `toBe`; `tenant-layer.ts` the same) are delivered; the composed form, its constructor and its recogniser — what E2 imports — are delivered; nothing shipped presumes the case-set. The card's literal acceptance grep ("hits the spec file only") is met in its intent and not in its letter, because of prose hits that predate the PR; the seat's reading is the right one.

**D. Engine seat 2's two requests (6123462901):** item 2 (by-reference returns, `toBe` pins) accepted and delivered; item 1 half delivered (composed form) and half re-routed (C above). Right.

**What clears the FAIL:** one patch round on this branch fixing A1 (preferably remedy (a), with its pin) and A2's three wordings, regenerating nothing (TSDoc and a changeset line only; `api-surface` and `export-origins` are unaffected, unless remedy (a) is taken, which changes no export), and a new record at the new head. Everything else in this PR passes this review as it stands.

Reviewed-by: `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
